articleTitle: Multipath and imaging problems in GPS receiver antennas
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This report outlines several wave propagation phenomena which affect electronic navigation and positioning systems and describes the significance of these phenomena and possible means of identifying the effects as they may appear in field operation. The main emphasis of this report concerns GPS applications but the conclusions are directly applicable to many other code/phase radio positioning and navigation systems.

articleTitle: The extended aperture field integration method and its linearity in calculating the radiation pattern of reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A symmetric paraboloidal reflector with a dipole feed is considered. An aperture plane is selected in front of the reflector and at different distances from its edge. The aperture field is calculated as a summation of the fields due to the direct, reflected and edge diffracted rays and the contribution of slope diffraction and caustic correction terms. In order to Increase the amount of the edge diffracted rays intercepted by the aperture, the aperture size is extended beyond the physical aperture of the reflector. The far-zone radiation pattern is obtained using Fourier transform of the total aperture field. The effects of the aperture location and aperture size on the radiation pattern are studied and presented. Also, the linearity of the extended aperture field integration method is investigated.

articleTitle: Cross-polarization on the aperture of a compact range using dual parabolic cylindrical reflectors
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The cross-polarization over the projected aperture of dual parabolic cylindrical reflectors employed as a compact range is studied. It is found that the level of the cross-polar component of the aperture field depends on the geometry of the two reflectors, the feed orientation and the feed polarization. The effects of these parameters on the cross-polarization level of the compact range are investigated and some representative results axe presented.

articleTitle: The quadrifilar helix as a GPS receiver antenna
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The expected limit of accuracy of the Global Positioning System (GPS) is of the order of the dimensions of the antenna in use.which translates into the centimeter range at GPS frequencies of 1.2–1.6 GHz. In these instances, phase-derived position determination is affected by the antenna phase centre movement which in turn is a function of the observation angle. The circularly polarized short quadrifilar helix is compact and lightweight and is one of the antennas presently used with GPS receivers. Both the amplitude and phase characteristics of this antenna are studied to determine its suitability for various GPS applications such as in hydrography and aviation where peculiar constraints may be placed upon the near-and-below-horizon response.

articleTitle: Hybrid mode analysis of a conical waveguide with a radially tapered impedance wall
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This article presents a new conical structure which can support the spherical hybrid modes associated with corrugated conical waveguide. The analysis closely follows that of hybrid modes in corrugated conical waveguide. It is found that in order to obtain hybrid modes in a dielectric lined conical waveguide it is necessary to taper the dielectric constant of the lining.

articleTitle: Equivalent skin-effect parameters of lossy coaxial cables for transient analysis
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new equivalent circuit is derived for a coaxial cable, taking into account the transient skin-effect. This model is required for analysis involving high speed digital or high frequency signal transmission. The model can be also applied where coaxial cables are studied for electromagnetic pulse (EMP) induced transients and the impact produced in electronic circuits. The solution for the transient field problem is obtained by using the Laplace transform applied to the Maxwell's equations in time domain. Numerical results showed that when very fast phenomena (such as EMP) have to be characterized the transient skin-effect is very important.

articleTitle: The field distribution near a caustic and its application to the analysis of high frequency em backscattering from dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It is well known that for simple-shaped dielectric bodies with certain range of refractive index, a significant amount of incident electromagnetic energy may be backscattered towards the source due to a focusing phenomenon called the “glory-rays”. It has been found that the field predicted by geometrical optics to describe this phenomenon occupies a finite circular aperture, and exhibits one or more caustic “rings”, most notably along the outer perimeter of the aperture where the field is singular. In order to specify a finite value for the field at the caustic, as well as to provide a continuous transition from the lit to shadow regions as required by the physical considerations, the Huygens-Fresnel principle has been applied. The resulting expression obtains a frequency dependent finite value for the field at the caustic, and degenerates to the geometrical optics field at points removed from the caustic, in the lit region.

articleTitle: Comparison of surface impedance models for quasistationary electromagnetic field scatterers
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: General integral equations for quasistationary electromagnetic fields have been derived and an improved surface impedance model for conducting objects has been proposed. These equations have a simple structure and the amount of computation for their solution is substantially reduced with respect to that corresponding to the general electromagnetic field integral equations. The proposed modelling technique is applied to a test example and yields highly accurate results, even within the range of parameters where models used so far are not applicable. It is particularly recommended for quasistationary fields in the presence of magnetic material conductors.

articleTitle: An analytical method solving a certain a certain class of inverse scattering problem
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Inverse scattering of an E-polarized cylindrical electromagnetic wave with an arbitrary amplitude distribution at a discontinuity created by an imperfect dielectric and coinciding with the transverse direction is solved rigorously by means of transformation into an equivalent plane wave(TEPW).

articleTitle: Scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by a ferrite shell
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by a ferrite cylindrical shell is investigated. It is solved as a boundary value problem in cylindrical coordinates. The effect of the shell wall thickness and the ferrite parameters on the scattered field patterns and the scattering cross-section is determined.

articleTitle: Ferroelectric antenna for mobile communication systems
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Experimental results of the ferroelectric antenna proposed to be used for mobile communication system are included in this paper. Theory of linear dielectric antenna excited by HE11 mode is included for optimal analysis of this structure for improved performance of the antenna composed of ferroelectrics that come into the category of non-linear dielectrics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from dielectric bodies of revolution: Theoretical and experimental results
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering of electromagnetic waves from dielectric bodies of revolution in the resonance region is considered. A theoretical solution to the problem is formulated in terms of equivalent currents on the surface of the scatterer, leading to a set of surface integral equations which arc solved numerically using the method of moments. The procedure is applied to dielectric bodies of revolution of various sizes and shapes which simulate ice, and for which experimental results of the backscattering matrix elements are available. Very good agreement between the numerical results and the experimental data is obtained.

articleTitle: On Wu's electromagnetic missile
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It is demonstrated that not only the spectral content but also the source geometry is essential to the existence of Wu' s electromagnetic missile. The relationship between the range of such a pulse and the geometrical parameters of the source distribution is given. Recent results on the slowly decaying fields generated by switching on a uniform distribution of source current at t = 0 are also presented.

articleTitle: On the inverse black body radiation problem
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A survey of the inverse black body radiation problem is presented including a modification to the Hamid-Ragheb approximation which leads to a new approximate formula for the Planck's radiation law valid at all frequencies. The modified regime is useful in solving the inverse black body radiation problem in closed form. The absolute percentage errors in constructing the area-coldness distribution due to the proposed and previous approximations are presented. The results suggest that our modified approximation to Planck's law is more suitable than all other approximations at all frequencies.

articleTitle: The behaviour of space deployable, non-paraboloidal reflector antennas and the morphology of aperture illumination phase in relation to the far field
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: 1) The one to one to one correspondance of the reflector shape to the aperture phase distribution then to the far-field pattern permits making an estimate of the effect of symmetric surface distortions on far-field patterns- Similar relationships can be expected for faceted reflectors as well. 2) Clearly as the number of gores (or facets) is increased, the effects of these distortions on the main beam structure is decreased and becomes evident only in the sidelobe structure. 3) It is evident that single scan (e.g. E-plane and/or H-plane) far-field patterns of such reflectors should not be used to characterize their behaviours since the scan can be chosen which could be misleadingly “good” or “bad”. The entire sectional plane contour plots are needed. Conversely, if in a particular application selective treatment of the beam illumination is needed, this might be achieved by an appropriate rotation of the reflector.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of a cylindrical dielectric-coated antenna with a circumferential airgap
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a cylindrical dielectric-coated antenna with a narrow circumferential airgap between the conductor and the inner surface of the dielectric layer is derived "by the equivalence principle. A comparison of the radiation pattern and radiation characteristics with those of the antenna with no airgap indicates that the presence of the airgap shifts the direction of the major lobe towards the axis. The half-power beamwidth of the major lobe appears to increase with the size of the airgap.

articleTitle: Design procedure for a pencil beam antenna using dual parabolic cylindrical reflectors
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A design procedure for pencil beam antennas using dual parabolic cylindrical reflectors is presented. Initially, the aperture length is determined according to the required beamwidths, and the reflector focal lengths are selected to yield the desirable beam ellipticity. The angle between the reflectors Is then optimized to minimize the cross-polarization level. The expressions necessary for determination of the reflector geometries, using the selected reflector focal lengths and the angle between them, are also provided. For this design procedure, the feed is assumed to be located on the main reflector or its extension.

articleTitle: Analysis of traveling-wave loaded dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Detailed analysis of the traveling-wave dipole is presented using recent accurate expressions for the current distribution along a multiply loaded dipole antenna. These expressions result from an extension of Hurd's Wiener-Hopf solution for the input admittance of long dipoles. An optimization routine is used to determine the proper loading and location to excite an outward traveling current wave along most of the length of the dipole. Results from this model agree favorably with previously reported experimental and theoretical data. The expressions derived give a better insight into the advantages of traveling-wave over standing-wave antennas as well as the feasibility of using active as well as passive loads.

articleTitle: Power loss due to radiation in a suspended microstrip structure
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Power loss due to radiation is important for compatibility analyses of microwave and millimeter-wave integrated circuits. In this,paper, the results of a full-wave spectral-domain analysis to evaluate the fundamental-mode power radiated from a suspended microstrip line are reported. Measures for minimizing the radiation loss are recommended.

articleTitle: Estimation of the electromagnetic field in sea with rough upper and lower surfaces
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We present intial results from the investigation of the effect of roughness of both upper and lower sea surfaces on electromagnetic wave propagation in sea. The sea has been considered in terms of a three layered media (air-sea water-ground). Sea waves lead to the variations which occur in both upper and lower sea surfaces. These variations were studied using the perturbation technique. The problem is evaluated mathematically using the Residue and Saddle point methods.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic correlation in two channel radar systems: Theory and measurement at linear polarization
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In remote sensing of precipitation many conventional radars measure only the intensity of the backscattered radiation, often at linear polarization of fixed orientation. Over the last few years there has been increased interest in radars with more capabilities. Polarization diversity radars are capable of decomposing the received wave into two mutually orthogonal components, and thus more of the information content of the backscattered wave can be exploited. The National Research Council of Canada polarization diversity radars, situated in Ottawa, are capable of measuring the backscattered powers at two orthogonal polarizations, and they also measure the complex correlation between these two received components.

articleTitle: Multi-section transmission line transformer of arbitrary length
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A simple approach for matching a purely resistive load impedance to a given transmission line is presented. The parameters of the transformer can be accurately computed from presented equations. In this approach, the length of each section, as well as the characteristic impedance, can be properly chosen in order to minimize the total length of two sections while obtaining relatively wider bandwidth compared with the case of two sections of equal length. This approach provides much shorter total length and reduces the insertion loss of the matching section, while providing almost the same bandwidth property as compared with a single quarter-wavelength transformer section.

articleTitle: A simple method of calculating electromagnetic fields in solid conductors
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The distribution of the electromagnetic field quantities inside a good conductor is determined by assuming approximate boundary conditions at the conductor surface. These conditions are those corresponding to the exterior-field solution, obtained on the basis of an appropriate surface impedance model for the conducting body. The field inside a linear, isotropic and homogeneous conductor can be expressed directly in terms of the Green function for an unbounded space, corresponding to the conductor material characteristics. The proposed method is applied to a test example and yields accurate results even for high levels of penetration of the field into the conductor.

articleTitle: More improvement in the method of moments in the solution of Pocklington's and Hallen's intergral equations
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel numerical method is presented to solve Pocklington's and Hallen's integral equations using the method of moments applying extended boundary condition and kernel expansion. The kernel expansion used is the well known finite Fourier consine series with period of 2L where L is the antenna length. Current expansion is chosen as entire domain bases. The selection of the weighting functions and inner product domain are such that more simplification is reached. Hence the numerical computation of the impedance matrix is fairly fast and simple. Results obtained by this method agree with experimental and previous published ones.

articleTitle: Synthesis of line feeds for conical reflectors
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The matched feed concept is used to determine the electrical characteristics of a line source feed for conical reflector antennas. A linearly polarized plane wave incident on the reflector is used to determine the field distribution along and in the vicinity of the focal axis of the reflector. The co-polar, cross-polar and the axial field components are determined and their dependence on the reflector size and the radial distance is studied. The results indicate that for a line source of finite diameter its surface field distribution must contain other field components to generate a linearly polarized far field.

articleTitle: Radom depolarizing factors in an earth station-satellite link
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An expression for the cross polar discrimination in a ground-satellite link, in which the random depolarizing factors are taken into consideration is derived. It is observed that the down-link on the average offers a better XPD all the time. The difference is about 1.5 dB at the most. This difference diminishes with increase in the visibility.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical investigation of stacked circular microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The impedance bandwidth and radiation patterns of the stacked circular microstrip antennas are investigated. Both dominant TM11 and the higher TM21 modes of operation are considered and the effect of feed point location, the separation of the patches on the return loss and the radiation patterns are studied. Sample results are presented graphically.

articleTitle: Feed tilt for optimization of sidelobe levels in offset paraboloids
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Use of offset reflectors of small F/D ratios is limited by their high sidelobe characteristics in the symmetric plane and poor cross polar performance in the asymmetric plane [1]. Jamnejad-Dailami and Rahmat-Samii [2] have noticed improvement in the symmetric plane sidelobe level by orienting the axis of the prime-focus feed along the direction of an incident ray, for which the reflected ray from the antenna passes through the centre of the projected aperture, (this direction is referred to as the central aperture direction in the remaining text). However, tilting the feed axis from the axis of the cone generating the reflector surface from the parent paraboloid deteriorates, to some degree, the co-polar sidelobe level and the peak cross polarization in the asymmetric plane.

articleTitle: Improving the accuracy of the aperture integration method by a proper choice of the numerical integration technique
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A uniformly illuminated circular aperture is considered and the radiation pattern is computed using the aperture field integration method. For the integration algorithms three different methods of FFT, Simpson's rule and the Guass-Legendre are used. To compare the accuracy of these different techniques, the same integration is also performed analytically. It is shown that the Guass-Legendre technique is the most accurate one and the FFT is the second.

articleTitle: A waveguide array antenna for remote sensing applications
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A waveguide array is designed, which consists of one hundred radiating waveguide elements. The array is mounted inside a sectoral horn to shape its vertical pattern. In the array plane, the element excitation is designed to yield sidelobes around or less than 30 dB level. Its beamwidths in the vertical and horizontal planes are required to be larger than fifteen degrees and less than one degree, respectively. The unit is designed to be used as a remote sensing radar antenna for investigation of ice reflectivity in northern waters.

articleTitle: Antenna scattering by masts and towers
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Although situations involving antennas on towers and masts may be solved individually to-day by moment methods with a high degree of precision, there is still a need for more general methods.

articleTitle: The microstrip antenna with finite ground plane for use with satellite positioning systems
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the use of satellite positioning systems such as the Global Positioning System (GPS) significant errors can be introduced into the indicated position through the properties of the antenna structure. Of particular interest are the phase characteristics of the antenna as a function of observation angle. The microstrip antenna features a rugged, low profile and light weight construction making it an ideal choice for practical applications, but positioning accuracy may be limited by the mounting surface.

articleTitle: On the mutual coupling in planar microstrip arrays
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Simplified theory and its numerical computation are presented for the inclusion of the mutual coupling in the planar array theory of microstrip antennas of the circular disc patch type or the rectangular patch type. Although more rigorous treatments may be developed in the future or extended to other shapes, the purpose of the present task is to seek the most compact and simplified approach that still provides an efficient model for numerical analysis and that the approximations invoked are acceptable in most practical cases of analysis or synthesis routine for the above mentioned types of array. The main approximations adopted are: neglecting the surface waves, accepting the emperical extension formula for the reactive loading of the radiating apertures and the corresponding effective permittivity in the case of the transmission line model for the rectangular patch array. The formulation is programmed only for the cases of thin apertures that justify the modelling of the magnetic ribbon current by a radiating line current in order to reduce the computation time.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave propagation along multiple conductor structures above a lossy earth
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In order to construct the 2N-port transfer function of an N conductor transmission line above a dissipative ground, the evaluation of the Sommerfeld integrals becomes imperative. Since the integrand of the integral, excluded in Carson's formulation, exhibits a pair of first order poles, a significantly different solution to the customary transmission line dispersion equations is obtained and an addition solution becomes mathematically feasible in the neighbourhood of the poles. Numerical methods prove to be time consuming and the existing analytical approximations either ignore the additional solution or are valid only for the special case of a single conductor. An unrestricted analytical expression is presented for the general solution of the transmission line equations. A comparison between the new analytical form and standard numerical integration techniques is provided as well as a comparison to the case of a single conductor available in the literature.

articleTitle: Application of diffraction techniques in propagation path loss modelling
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Diffraction techniques are used to predict the propagation path loss between a radio transmitter site and receiver sites located in the shadow of mountainous and hilly terrain. These predictions are used to determine the effective coverage range for a radio paging service and, in the reverse problem, are used to determine the required transmitter power and siting for a desired geographical coverage. Extensive field tests at over 100 sites and ranges to 50 km are summarized for comparison with predicted values.

articleTitle: Communication in a three rough layered conducting media
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of communication in the sea has been considered as propagation of radio waves in three layered media (air-sea-ground). The variations which may occur in the shape of the upper and lower surfaces, due to sea waves are considered. The effect of these variations is studied by using the perturbation method. The results obtained are compared with those mentioned elsewhere.

articleTitle: The co- and cross-polarized radiation patterns of a log-periodic slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The log-periodic slot antenna (LPSA) may be considered a dual of a familiar log-periodic dipole antenna only if the ground plane is infinite in size. If the ground plane is finite, the radiation pattern has been shown [1] to be an end-fire difference pattern.

articleTitle: A microprocessor-based monopulse phased array
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Although the basic principle of monopulse phased array is well known, this paper describes a new method designed to automatically search for an unknown source in the presence of strong RF interference.

articleTitle: Integral solution for the diffraction by a double cylindrical wedge
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new technique based on the spectrum of cylindrical waves and successive scattering is developed to evaluate the scattered field due to two parallel cylindrical scatterers to any desired degree of accuracy. The salient features of the method are discussed and the results are presented for some practical configurations, namely two parallel circular cylinders and two semi-infinite wedges. The proposed technique is also applicable for scattering by multiple bodies of arbitrary cross-sectional shape once the scattering by each body in isolation is manageable. The numerical results for the scattering by two cylinders agree with the available exact boundary value solution, whereas for the double wedge the transmission coefficient compares favorably with the exact values for the special case of a slit geometry and with two other asymptotic solutions for wide separations.

articleTitle: Scattering and transmission properties for a class of two-dimensional double bodies
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattered field from two cylindrical bodies due to an incident E-polarized plane wave is evaluated numerically using an integral equation for the surface currents and is solved by a modified method of moments. The multiple scattering by two parallel conducting circular cylinders as well as the diffraction by a double wedge with non-sharp edges are considered. The total scattered field from two parallel cylinders is divided into two components, namely the non-interaction term and a term due to all interactions between the cylinders. The non-interaction term is expressed exactly, whereas the interaction field is evaluated using the method of moments. It is found that this technique leads to an efficient solution for the scattering by cylinders of large radii. The computational advantages of this technique over classical boundary value and ordinary method of moments solutions are presented. Furthermore, the analysis for the diffraction by a two-dimensional aperture with arbitrary cross-section shape given by Morita is used to solve for the diffraction by a double wedge with non-sharp edges. Numerical results for the diffracted field and the transmission coefficient of a thin slit, thick slit, double truncated wedge and double capped wedge are also presented and compared with other available solutions.

articleTitle: Radiation from a long dipole antenna in the presence of infinitely long circular cylinder
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation from a long dipole in the presence of an infinitely long circular conducting parallel cylinder is examined analytically, The expression for the far-zone field, which includes all successive multiple scattering terms between the dipole and the cylinder, is derived using an iterative approximate procedure. The current induced on the dipole due to backscattering from the cylinder is calculated for each iteration. The derivation includes integral expressions which are solved asymptotically using the far-zone field approximations. Also a numerical technique is employed for solving the problem in order to verify the analytical solution. The results due to both analytical and numerical solutions are in excellent agreement with each other. It is also found that the interaction between the dipole and the cylinder has a significant effect on the radiation field.

articleTitle: Recent advances in dipole antenna analysis and design
publicationTitle: 1986 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Hurd's Wiener-Hopf solution for the input admittance of long dipoles is extended to the general case when the antenna is multiply fed and multiply loaded. Accurate expressions are thus derived for the radiation pattern, current distribution and input admittance of the arbitrarily fed and multiply loaded dipole antenna. Comparison with numerical methods as well as available experimental is presented. An optimization routine is employed to study the possibility of improving the radiation pattern using the technique of multiple excitation along the antenna with locations and complex values of the feed voltages as optimization parameters. The same study is done when the antenna is multiply loaded, where real values of the impedances are allowed to become negative to investigate the feasibility of using active elements as well as passive ones. A. modification in the transistor circuitry that is located at an optimal location long the active loop monopole antenna achieves resonance at a lower frequency than previously reported.
